p3.example: She committed to a well-rounded education combining vocational and postgraduate concepts.

p4.en: A method of studying where you do not attend a school or university in person.
p4.ex1: Distance learning increasingly offers the same well-rounded education as in-person study.
p4.ex2: He found distance learning rewarding but struggled with isolation and homesickness.
p4.example: She chose distance learning for flexibility while completing her postgraduate degree.

p4.en: Not changing; set at a particular level or time.
p4.ex1: She found the fixed pace of the programme increasingly demotivating.
p4.ex2: In contrast to distance learning, in-person courses have a fixed orientation timetable.
p4.example: The fixed schedule of in-person study contrasted with the flexibility of distance learning.

p4.en: Able to speak a language smoothly and accurately.
p4.ex1: Being fluent increasingly helped her value the in-person conference experience.
p4.ex2: In contrast to homesick students, fluent speakers adapted more quickly.
p4.example: She became fluent in the language of instruction through distance learning.

p4.en: To employ someone for a job.
p4.ex1: He was hired increasingly on the basis of his well-rounded, postgraduate education.
p4.ex2: In contrast to fixed roles, she was hired for a rewarding, flexible position.
p4.example: The university hired her as a distance learning tutor after graduation.

p4.en: Feeling sad because you are away from home.
p4.ex1: In contrast to distance learning, in-person study can leave students feeling homesick.
p4.ex2: He was homesick but valued the independence gained from studying abroad.
p4.example: She felt homesick during her first term abroad, despite the rewarding experience.

p4.en: The feeling of being sad because you miss home.
p4.ex1: She overcame homesickness by increasingly engaging with her fluent peers.
p4.ex2: In contrast to distance learning, in-person study can intensify homesickness.
p4.example: Homesickness and isolation were the main challenges of in-person study abroad.

p4.en: Used to show a clear difference between two things.
p4.ex1: She valued flexibility; in contrast, her peers preferred a fixed timetable.
p4.ex2: In contrast to homesickness, isolation is increasingly linked to distance learning.
p4.example: In contrast to distance learning, in-person study offers a fixed, structured environment.

p4.ex1: She became increasingly fluent as her confidence in the language grew.
p4.ex2: In contrast to fixed programmes, flexible distance learning is increasingly popular.
p4.example: Distance learning is increasingly seen as a rewarding alternative to in-person study.

p4.en: The state of being alone or separated from others.
p4.ex1: In contrast to in-person study, distance learning increasingly leads to isolation.
p4.ex2: She valued independence but struggled with the isolation of a fixed, remote programme.
p4.example: Isolation and homesickness were the main drawbacks of distance learning.

p4.en: More desirable or suitable than an alternative.
p4.ex1: In contrast to a fixed timetable, a flexible approach was preferable for her.
p4.ex2: A well-rounded education is preferable to an isolated, fixed distance learning experience.
p4.example: She found distance learning increasingly preferable due to its flexibility.

p4.en: Being in a particular place; or relating to now.
p4.ex1: In contrast to distance learning, in-person students are present for collaborative sessions.
p4.ex2: Being present increasingly helps students put theory into practice in real time.
p4.example: She was present at the in-person conference despite homesickness.

p4.en: Giving you a feeling of satisfaction or making you feel your efforts were worthwhile.
p4.ex1: Distance learning can be rewarding if you value flexibility over fixed structure.
p4.ex2: In contrast to demotivating isolation, a well-rounded programme is deeply rewarding.
p4.example: Despite isolation and homesickness, she found in-person study increasingly rewarding.

p4.en: To think that something is important and worth having.
p4.ex1: In contrast to fixed study, she valued the flexibility of a postgraduate distance programme.
p4.ex2: He valued the rewarding, hands-on experience of in-person study despite homesickness.
p4.example: She increasingly valued the independence gained through distance learning.
